Overview — main features & capabilities
- Base Account is a smart-wallet account layer + SDK that provides: universal sign‑in (SIWE), one‑tap USDC payments (Base Pay), onchain profile data collection, gasless/sponsored transactions (paymasters), batch/atomic transactions, sub‑accounts, and integrations with ecosystem libraries (wagmi, viem, OnchainKit, Privy, Mobile Wallet Protocol).
- Basenames: ENS‑style human readable names on Base. Fully onchain (built on ENS tech). Register/transfer/resolve names via base.org UI or programmatically via resolver ABI.
- Capabilities model: wallets expose per‑account, per‑chain capabilities via wallet_getCapabilities. Apps must detect capabilities before using advanced features (atomic batches, auxiliaryFunds / MagicSpend, paymasterService, dataCallback, flowControl, signInWithEthereum).
- Provider model: createBaseAccountSDK() yields an EIP‑1193 provider compatible with viem/wagmi. Provider routes requests to either the wallet UI, SDK-local handlers, or the configured RPC provider.

Key API methods & purposes
- SDK lifecycle
  - createBaseAccountSDK(options) — create SDK instance; returns sdk with getProvider() and subAccount manager.
    - Important options: appName, appLogoUrl, appChainIds, preference (attribution, telemetry), subAccounts.toOwnerAccount, paymasterUrls, telemetry (default true).
  - sdk.getProvider() — EIP‑1193 provider used for all wallet RPCs or to wrap into viem/wagmi.
- Payments
  - pay({ amount, to, testnet?, payerInfo?, callbackURL? }) — one‑tap USDC payment; returns payment id. Throws on failure.
  - getPaymentStatus({ id, testnet? }) — poll payment status: completed | pending | failed | not_found.
- Authentication & connection
  - wallet_connect (via provider.request) — connect and request capabilities (e.g., signInWithEthereum for SIWE). Returns accounts with capability results (message, signature).
  - eth_requestAccounts / eth_accounts — standard account connection.
- Batch & advanced transactions
  - wallet_sendCalls(params) — EIP‑5792 batch/atomic transaction submission. Supports capabilities object (paymasterService, dataCallback, etc.). Version "2.0.0".
  - wallet_getCallsStatus(callsId) — check batch status and receipts.
  - wallet_getCapabilities(account) — discover per‑chain capabilities (atomic, auxiliaryFunds, paymasterService, datacallback, flowControl).
- Sub Accounts
  - wallet_addSubAccount — create/import sub accounts for app-specific wallets.
  - wallet_getSubAccounts — fetch sub accounts for domain.
  - SDK convenience: sdk.subAccount.create(), .get(), .addOwner(), .setToOwnerAccount()
- Key & account utilities
  - generateKeyPair() / getKeypair() — P256 keypairs for Sub Accounts or other flows.
  - getCryptoKeyAccount() — get current crypto key account (webauthn or local) if present.
- Spend Permissions (SDK helpers)
  - requestSpendPermission(...) — generate & sign EIP‑712 spend permission.
  - fetchPermissions({account, chainId, spender, provider}) — list permissions.
  - getPermissionStatus(permission) — remaining spend, active flag.
  - prepareSpendCallData({permission, amount}) — returns call(s) for spender to execute (may include approveWithSignature + spend).
  - prepareRevokeCallData(permission) / requestRevoke(permission).
- UI components (account‑ui)
  - SignInWithBaseButton — prebuilt SIWE auth button (props: colorScheme, size, onClick/onSignInResult).
  - BasePayButton — prebuilt payment button (props: paymentOptions {amount,to,testnet,payerInfo}, styling props, onPaymentResult).

Essential usage patterns & examples
- Initialize SDK + provider (minimal)
  - const sdk = createBaseAccountSDK({ appName:'MyApp', appLogoUrl:'...', appChainIds:[base.id] });
  - const provider = sdk.getProvider();
- SIWE sign in (wallet_connect)
  - Generate nonce (crypto.randomUUID()), then:
    - const res = await provider.request({ method: 'wallet_connect', params:[{ version:'1', capabilities:{ signInWithEthereum: { nonce, chainId:'0x2105' } } }]});
    - Extract accounts[0].capabilities.signInWithEthereum => { message, signature } and verify on backend (viem.verifyMessage).
- One‑tap payment (pay)
  - const payment = await pay({ amount:'5.00', to:'0xRecipient', testnet:true });
  - const status = await getPaymentStatus({ id: payment.id, testnet:true });
  - Optionally request payer info with payerInfo.requests and a callbackURL to validate server‑side.
- Batch/atomic flows (wallet_sendCalls)
  - Build calls array (to, value, data), check wallet_getCapabilities(account) for atomic support, then:
    - const id = await provider.request({ method: 'wallet_sendCalls', params:[{ version:'2.0.0', from, chainId:'0x2105', atomicRequired:true, calls, capabilities:{ paymasterService: { url } } }]});
  - Poll with wallet_getCallsStatus(callsId).
- Sub Accounts (improved UX, fewer passkey prompts)
  - Use provider.request({ method:'wallet_getSubAccounts', params:[{ account, domain }]}) to fetch or wallet_addSubAccount to create.
  - For embedded wallets, set sdk.subAccount.setToOwnerAccount(() => toViemAccount({ wallet: embeddedWallet })) to delegate signing.
- Spend Permissions flow
  - permission = await requestSpendPermission({ account, spender, token, chainId, allowance, periodInDays, provider });
  - spendCalls = await prepareSpendCallData({ permission, amount });
  - Submit from spender account (wallet_sendCalls or eth_sendTransaction).
- Basenames resolver (OnchainKit / wagmi example)
  - Read resolver contract L2ResolverAbi; compute reverse node (convertReverseNodeToBytes) and call name() to get basename; fetch text records / avatar using resolver ABI.

Important configuration options & best practices
- createBaseAccountSDK options
  - appName, appLogoUrl, appChainIds (which chains your app supports)
  - preference: attribution.auto | dataSuffix; telemetry: true|false (opt-out)
  - subAccounts.toOwnerAccount: provide function that returns owner account (embedded/local) for sub-account signing
  - paymasterUrls: map chainId → paymaster URL (for default sponsorship)
- Capabilities detection: always call wallet_getCapabilities(account) and adapt UX (atomicRequired, include paymasterService, consider auxiliaryFunds).
- Data collection: dataCallback capability requires HTTPS callbackURL (ngrok allowed in dev), server must return either { request: ... } on success or { errors: ... } to prompt user corrections. Optional fields via optional:true.
- Telemetry: on by default; can be disabled via SDK option telemetry:false.
- Popup behavior: ensure click-to-open popups (avoid extra async logic between click and provider request). COOP header: use unsafe-none or same-origin-allow-popups. Wallet popup lingers 200ms to accept quick follow-up requests.
- Error handling: common codes — 4001 (user rejected), 4100 (method not supported), -32602 (invalid params). Always wrap provider.request in try/catch.
- Basenames specifics: transfer requires signing four transactions (ownership, management, address resolution, NFT send) using the Basenames UI; do not transfer via marketplaces (OpenSea) as that only moves the NFT, not management/resolution.

Core concepts & architecture (concise)
- SDK ↔ Wallet Service ↔ Smart Wallet Contracts:
  - Frontend calls provider.request (EIP‑1193). SDK may open wallet popup/mobile deep link to Wallet Service (passkey/session keys).
  - Wallet Service issues session keys, signs userOps (ERC‑4337), optionally uses paymaster (ERC‑7677) for gas sponsorship or auxiliaryFunds/MagicSpend for Coinbase balances.
  - Smart Wallet contracts (ERC‑4337) are deployed on supported chains; sub‑accounts are child smart wallets linked onchain.
- Provider routing rules (what is handled where)
  - provider requests either: sent to wallet app (signing, wallet_sendCalls, wallet_connect, subAccount RPCs), handled locally by SDK (eth_requestAccounts/eth_accounts/eth_chainId etc.), or forwarded to RPC provider (eth_getBalance, block queries, eth_call).
- Capabilities-driven feature gating: wallets advertise capabilities per chain/account; apps should detect and adapt (progressive enhancement).

Developer integrations & tooling
- Wagmi: use baseAccount connector or custom provider transport (custom(provider)). Example wagmi config shows coinbaseWallet connector preference 'smartWalletOnly'.
- Privy: integrated provider + embedded wallets; supports sub‑accounts and toViemAccount bridging.
- OnchainKit: Identity component and utilities (e.g., convertReverseNodeToBytes) to resolve basenames.
- Mobile: Mobile Wallet Protocol Client (EIP‑1193 provider / wagmi connector) for React Native.

UX / operational notes
- Gas: smart wallets cost more gas than EOAs; factor that into UX.
- MagicSpend (auxiliaryFunds): when present do not disable actions based on onchain balance alone.
- Paymasters: support ERC‑7677 endpoints (pm_getPaymasterStubData / pm_getPaymasterData / pm_getAcceptedPaymentTokens) for sponsored transactions, including ERC20 gas payments.
- Basename registration pricing and discounts, renewals, auctions, grace periods documented in Basenames FAQ.

Where to look in docs (quick map)
- Quickstarts: web, React, React Native, Wagmi
- Guides: Authenticate Users (SIWE), Accept Payments (pay/getPaymentStatus), Sub Accounts, Batch Transactions, Spend Permissions, Sponsor Gas (Paymasters)
- Reference: Provider RPC methods (wallet_connect, wallet_sendCalls, wallet_getCapabilities, etc.), SDK utilities (generateKeyPair, getCryptoKeyAccount), pay/getPaymentStatus, spend‑permission utilities
- UI: SignInWithBaseButton, BasePayButton, Brand Guidelines
